entities.summary:
Bolesław Januszowic (died 1424) was a prince of the Masovian Piast dynasty, the eldest son and intended heir of Janusz I the Elder, Duke of Warsaw. His unexpected death in 1424, preceding his long-reigning father, created a significant dynastic crisis within the fragmented Piast duchies of Masovia, ultimately altering the line of succession and contributing to the gradual integration of these territories into the larger Kingdom of Poland. As a member of a cadet branch of the Piast house, Bolesław's life, though cut short, illuminates the complex political landscape of late medieval Poland, characterized by intricate familial alliances and the persistent struggle for regional autonomy against the growing power of the Jagiellonian monarchy.

Born at an unknown date, Bolesław Januszowic was groomed as the successor to his father's vast Masovian territories, which included Warsaw, Ciechanów, and Nur. During his father's reign, Bolesław likely participated in the administration of the duchy, representing the ducal authority in local matters and participating in the regional sejmiks. He was married to Anna of Pynsk, a Lithuanian princess, a union that underscored the strategic political ties between Masovia and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, a crucial alliance in the region against the Teutonic Knights, and reflected the complex web of dynastic marriages common in the era.
